overloadMerges.note: Documented the semantic effect of the trailing '*' parameter (non-modal display) and the priority formData has over an associated form class, neither of which the mechanical draft's generic param entries conveyed.
overloadMerges.semanticRole: Presents a form (project/table form name, a .json path, or a form-description object) to the user, either modally (blocking until an accept/cancel action), or -- if the trailing '*' is passed -- non-modally in the last-opened window of the current process while execution continues immediately.

params.name: aTable
params.description: Table owning the form. If omitted, the default table is used, or a project form is expected.

params.name: form
params.description: Name of a table/project form, a POSIX path to a .json file describing the form, or an object describing the form.

params.name: formData
params.description: Object whose properties become available inside the form via the Form command. Takes priority over an associated form class: if formData is passed (and defined), the form class object is not instantiated. If omitted (or undefined) and no form class is associated, DIALOG creates a new empty object bound to the form.

params.name: useCurrentProcess
params.description: If passed, the form loads and displays in the last-open window of the current process; DIALOG returns immediately while the form remains active on screen, reacting normally to user actions until CANCEL/ACCEPT (or a standard action) closes it, or the process terminates.

constraints: A dialog is closed by an 'accept' action (ak accept, Enter, or ACCEPT) which sets OK to 1, or a 'cancel' action (ak cancel, Escape, or CANCEL) which sets OK to 0.
Validation is not saving: if the form includes fields, SAVE RECORD must be called explicitly to persist modified data.

When the trailing '*' is used, a window must already exist (created beforehand) -- the current dialog window or the default per-process window cannot be reused, otherwise error -9909 is generated. The window is closed automatically by 4D once the form is dismissed.
